#H1N1 Site Contents Vary by Strain and Study
The five H1 sites are Sa, Sb, Ca1, Ca2, and Cb, and their residue counts differ between the classical PR8 map and pandemic strains.
For instance in a comparison study between 2009 pandemic and eurasian avian-like strains, the sites were of sizes 13, 12, 11, 8, and 5 residues respectively.
Site differences between the two strains were at 4 (Sa), 6 (Sb), 6 (Ca1), 4 (Ca2), and 2 (Cb).
A single H128N substitution in Sa was sufficient to cause a four-fold HI change and measurable antigenic drift

Some papers don't uniformly cover all sites
Eg. Pandemic H1N1 paper escape-mutant sequencing covered only Sa, Sb, Ca2, and added a new site called Pa
Assignments:
Sa: 141, 142, 143, 171, 172, 174, 177, 180
Sb: 170, 173, 202, 206, 210, 211, 212
Ca2: 51, 154, 156, 157, 158, 159, 200, 238
Pa: 147


#H3N2 sites
These were assembled using monoclonal antibody competition and escape mutant selection instead of a fixed residue roster

#Why Yean's numbers are strange
The papers used don't report the same thing.
Gupta et al. and Pan & Deem defined these epitope regions for general use. This was specially used for computing antigenic distance.
These regions were deliberately enlarged and mapped onto a model strain.
Conversely the classical A-E ranges were structures defined on the H3 model.
We guessed right: the discontinuity was due to those sites being clusters of surface-exposed residues, exposed by the protein folding.
Overall the fraction of substitutions in the epitope dominating the mutations calculate well for antigenic distance and vaccine efficacy estimations; correlation weakens when the whole hemagglutinin is used
